I ran the `/code-conventions --review-pr` checklist against the diff and found nine convention issues. None is a blocker. The two I'd fix first are the mixed small-screen detection in `PendingRequestsTable.tsx` and the tests that can't fail. The checklist covers 78 rules and I considered each one; these applied: FEAT-01, CODE-02, CODE-04, UX-01, PROD-01, TEST-01, TEST-02 and TEST-05, plus the written web testing and conventions rules. I didn't need to look up past review learnings for any rule, and I left the code unchanged. Generating the checklist wrote `docs/engineering/pr-self-review-checklist.generated.md`, and I marked every item checked in it. That file sits in the already-untracked `docs/engineering/` folder, so no tracked file changed. ## Findings **1. Medium: two different ways of detecting small screens in one folder** `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceAddressBook/PendingRequestsTable.tsx:40` - `PendingRequestsTable` uses MUI's `useMediaQuery(theme.breakpoints.down('lg'))`, which switches at about 1200px. - The table next to it, `SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx:57`, uses the repo's `useIsMobile()` (`@/hooks/use-mobile`), which switches at 768px. - These two tables are tabs on the same page, so the Pending tab and the Contacts tab change layout at different widths. - **Fix:** use `useIsMobile`, or plain Tailwind responsive widths such as `w-[15%] lg:w-[20%]`. Either way the MUI imports in a shadcn/Tailwind component go away. **2. Low: the same condition is repeated in three class names** `PendingRequestsTable.tsx:107-109` - `isSmallScreen ? '…' : '…'` appears in three header cells. Tailwind breakpoint classes would remove the JS branching entirely (CODE-04). **3. Low: the full "Requested by" address may not fit its column** `PendingRequestsTable.tsx:175-184` - The full address (`shortAddress={false}`) now sits in a column that is 20% wide, about 144px at the new 720px minimum table width. - The trigger is `inline-flex min-w-0` but nothing truncates the text, so it will likely wrap or overflow (UX-01). The tooltip shows the full value anyway, so the cell could use a short address or a `truncate` class. **4. Low: repeated wrapper and near-duplicate branches** `PendingRequestsTable.tsx:131,175` - The `
` wrapper now appears twice here and again in `SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx`. - The two `requestedBy` branches differ only in a few props (CODE-02). A small `FullAddress` helper, or computing the props once, would keep them from drifting apart. **5. Low: a shared component changed without a stated product decision** `apps/web/src/features/myAccounts/components/AccountItem/AccountItemChainBadge.tsx:26` - Removing the "Multichain account on:" heading changes the multichain tooltip everywhere this badge is used. It is exported through `features/myAccounts/feature.ts`, not only in the address book. - That is a visible behaviour change outside the PR's stated address-book scope (PROD-01). The PR description should reference the design decision. **6. Low: a test assertion that can never fail** `apps/web/src/features/myAccounts/components/AccountItem/__tests__/AccountItemChainBadge.test.tsx:42` - The single-chain test asserts that "Multichain account on:" is absent. The single-chain branch never rendered that heading, so the check passes with or without this change (TEST-01). - Also, `Tooltip*` is mocked as a plain `div`, so the multichain test doesn't show the content lives inside the tooltip. Checking that there is exactly one `multichain-tooltip` would be stronger. **7. Low: the SafeItem test fixture is hand-written** `AccountItemChainBadge.test.tsx:20-27` - `createSafeItem` fills in a hard-coded address and fixed values. The repo already has `safeItemBuilder()` in `apps/web/src/tests/builders/safeItem.ts` (TEST-05). - **Fix:** `safeItemBuilder().with({ chainId }).build()`. **8. Low: tests don't check the new behaviour they describe** - `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceAddressBook/__tests__/SpaceAddressBookTable.test.tsx:170-175`: the test "exposes the full name via a tooltip trigger" only checks that the trigger button exists. It never checks the tooltip content. The web test guide asks for the strongest assertion that matches the test name. - `PendingRequestsTable.test.tsx`: the small-screen column widths and the new `showHasMore`/`maxVisible={3}` on `NetworkLogosList` have no tests, and the `NetworkLogosList` mock drops those props (TEST-02). **9. Low: the new test imports `render` from the wrong place** `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceAddressBook/__tests__/PendingRequestsTable.test.tsx:1` - It imports `render` from `@testing-library/react`. The written web rule (`docs/engineering/conventions/web/project-structure.md`, Testing) says to use `@/tests/test-utils`. - Most tests next to it break the same rule, so this follows local habit. It still breaks the documented rule; `AccountItemChainBadge.test.tsx` in the same PR does it correctly. The new cross-feature imports (`@/features/multichain`) go through the public entry point, so FEAT-01 passes.
